name: Papercut Art
author: TBIT DESIGN - Thomas Breher
description: Layered paper pictures with real depth - the papercut look, computed entirely in your browser. A picture is a stack of paper with one light between the sheets, and everything in it is a THING you can grab: click it, drag it anywhere, turn it, resize it by its corners, roll a new variation, or punch it out of the paper so it becomes a hole onto what lies behind. One list shows the whole stack from front to back, and you drag a row to move a thing deeper or nearer - there is no layer to administer, no nesting and no arrows. Every thing carries its own paper colour. Nothing is baked in, nothing is locked to a horizon, and Ctrl+Z always leads back. IT STARTS WITH YOUR PICTURE: opening the studio takes the document you are working on and slices it along its DEPTH into up to twenty layers, using the editor's own local depth model - so what ends up in front really was in front, instead of merely being brighter. Each sheet can take its colour straight from the photo, and the local subject cutout lifts a person or product onto the front layer. Nothing is uploaded anywhere; without the model the picture is sliced by brightness instead, and it still works. OR BUILD A SCENE: parametric landscapes that reroll with every seed (alpine ridges, rolling hills, dunes, scalloped water, a city skyline with setbacks and spires), procedural forests of conifers, broadleaf, birches and palms with the height variation you choose, patches of grass, reeds, meadow flowers and boulders, cumulus clouds you can billow and fray, a sun with as many rays as you like, a full moon or a crescent, corner branches with leaves, your own words in real paper letters - with real counters in the a, d and o - and TWENTY-THREE animal silhouettes traced from PUBLIC-DOMAIN originals: deer, moose, fox, hare, bear, wolf, cat, dog, owl, horse, squirrel, boar, ibex, robin, gull, whale and dolphin on the ground, plus soaring eagle, heron, gulls, songbirds, owl and butterfly in the sky. THE LOOK runs on three dials rather than a list of names: the colour comes from a palette or from your photo, the paper is smooth or fibrous, and the sheets are separated by a deep soft shadow or a narrow hard rim. Eight ready looks sit on top of them, from an all-white lightbox over sunset and forest to a night glow, and brand-kit colours fit right in. THE PASSEPARTOUT is a thing like everything else: a sheet of paper with a window punched out of it, sitting at the very front. Circle, oval, heart, arch, hexagon, rectangle, an initial letter, or one of the three you shape yourself - a star with as many points and as much bite as you like, an elliptical ring you can set the width and lean of, and two rings reaching into each other. Whatever else you drop on that same sheet becomes part of it: birds left and right, or your own words cut clean through the paper, several lines under each other in one block. Sixteen ready scenes to start from, and one shared light you drag to set every shadow. Insert as a group of editable layers, one per sheet of paper.
